title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.5-7): Grothendieck is building a topological model, the 'isotopic category', for the anabelian dictionary. Objects are oriented surfaces of finite type (g,ν). Morphisms are isotopy classes of finite étale maps. He wants to show that every such class f: X→Y factors canonically as an isotopy-class isomorphism X ≅ Y' followed by a finite covering Y'→Y. Uniqueness reduces (previous page, (11)) to a rigidity statement: if γ is a finite-order automorphism (a deck transformation) of an anabelian surface and γ is isotopic to the identity, then γ = id.

Argument on this page:
(i) Replace γ by an automorphism preserving a complex-algebraic structure of type (g,ν) on X. A single periodic homeomorphism of a surface preserves some conformal structure, by the classical Kerékjártó–Eilenberg / Nielsen realization for cyclic groups.
(ii) Assume 2g+ν≥2 (the page reads '2g-ν≥2', surely a misreading). Then the open curve X embeds by Abel–Jacobi into its generalized (Rosenlicht) Jacobian J. This J is an extension of the abelian variety Jac(X̄) by a torus of dimension ν-1.
(iii) γ is isotopic to the identity, so it acts trivially on H_1(X) = H_1(J). Hence the induced automorphism of J has trivial linear part, i.e. it is a translation. That translation is by a torsion point, since γ has finite order.
(iv) So it suffices that, in the anabelian case 2g-2+ν>0, X ⊂ J is stable under no nonzero translation. Grothendieck calls this 'well known' and adds that a purely topological proof should be easy.

Then: finite étale covers of anabelian surfaces are anabelian. This gives the Corollary: for Y anabelian, each isotopy class of finite étale maps X→Y is a right torsor under A°_X, the group of homeomorphisms of X isotopic to the identity. The next page completes the proof via Prop. 2 and deduces:
- the components of the space of finite étale maps X→Y are contractible (via Earle–Eells contractibility of A°_X);
- the Teichmüller group T_X acts on Hom_ext(X,Y) with finite stabilizers, namely the deck groups Aut_Y(Y'_f);
- the orbits correspond to isomorphism classes of finite covers of Y homeomorphic to X.
errors: The condition written '2g-ν≥2' must be a misreading or slip for 2g+ν≥2. That is what is needed for X to embed in its generalized Jacobian: (0,2) and (1,0) embed, with ν counting punctures. The anabelian condition itself is 2g-2+ν>0.
Step (i) is asserted without proof ('on peut supposer'). It is true by the classical Kerékjártó/Eilenberg theorem on periodic surface homeomorphisms, or Nielsen realization for cyclic groups.

The key fact (iv) is only cited as 'bien connu', so the proof is incomplete as written. It holds, e.g. via Lefschetz on X̄: a nonzero torsion translation is fixed-point free, but an automorphism isotopic to the identity on X̄ fixing the ν≥1 punctures has Lefschetz number 2-2g. The cases g≥2 and g=1 with ν≥1 need checking separately. Alternatively use Hurwitz/Serre faithfulness on H_1.
Numbering inconsistency: the text says 'Compte tenu de la proposition 1', while the next page invokes 'prop. 2' for the rigidity statement proved here.

ideas.what: A finite-order homeomorphism of an anabelian (hyperbolic) surface that is isotopic to the identity is the identity, i.e. finite groups inject into the mapping class group
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of finite subgroups into the mapping class group (Hurwitz; Serre's level-3 lemma; Nielsen)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hurwitz, Nielsen, Serre (1960); standard, e.g. in Farb–Margalit
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme discussions of the Teichmüller tower; not explicitly proved there

ideas.what: Proof via an invariant algebraic structure plus Abel–Jacobi embedding into the generalized Jacobian: γ acts by a torsion translation, and an anabelian curve admits no nonzero stabilizing translation
ideas.modern_name: Rosenlicht generalized Jacobian / Albanese argument for rigidity of automorphisms of open curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Rosenlicht, Serre's 'Groupes algébriques et corps de classes'); the specific route is a variant of standard proofs

ideas.what: Isotopy classes of finite étale maps X→Y are A°_X-torsors; components of the space of étale maps are contractible; T_X acts on Hom_ext(X,Y) with finite stabilizers equal to deck groups, with orbits indexed by isomorphism classes of covers
ideas.modern_name: Topological/isotopic category of surfaces as model for outer homomorphisms of surface groups; Teichmüller groupoid foundations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; implicit in work on the Teichmüller tower (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura) and the anabelian section of Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and anabelian ideas, but not this 'isotopic category' formalism in detail

missed.claim: An early, explicit formalization of an 'isotopic category' of topological surfaces with finite étale maps, intended as the topological counterpart of the anabelian category of outer homomorphisms. The finite-stabilizer and torsor statements are standard facts, but this organization as foundations for Galois action on Teichmüller predates the Esquisse.
missed.quote: toute classe d'isotopie de morphismes finis étales de X dans Y est un torseur à droite sous le groupe A°_X des automorphismes de X isotopes à l'identité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents how Grothendieck set up the topological side of anabelian geometry around 1978, before the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct but classical: rigidity of finite-order mapping classes, and torsor/finite-stabilizer consequences. The generalized-Jacobian proof route is a mildly unusual choice but not new. The value is historical (the early isotopic-category formalism), not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: 'par prolongement analogue de l'hypothèse homologique' is likely 'par conséquent, en vertu de l'hypothèse homologique' (or similar). The sense is that, since γ acts trivially on homology, it induces a translation.
'tout revêtement étale fini' is correct in sense; the margin addition reads 'top' (surface topologique anabélienne).
In the Corollary, the inserted phrase is '{Y anabélienne}' replacing a struck-through 'deux'.
